day_1: Welcome! Let's start with system design. How do you approach structuring a FastAPI project for high maintainability and validation using Pydantic?
Can you explain how you handle input validation errors in FastAPI and ensure client-facing error responses are clean and structured?
day_2: Walk me through the core Python data structures you reach for most in backend work, and when each one is the right choice.
How would you use a generator pipeline to process a large file line by line without loading it all into memory?
day_3: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous code in Python, and how does asyncio allow concurrent tasks?
Why are dataclasses useful for modeling domain entities, and how do they compare to plain dictionaries?
day_4: How do you structure route dependencies and request validation in FastAPI to keep endpoint handlers clean?
What happens when Pydantic validation fails in a request body, and how would you customize the error response format?
day_5: How do you write reliable async tests with pytest, and how do you mock external HTTP calls?
Explain how fixtures and coverage metrics help you keep a test suite healthy.
day_6: How do you design an in-memory session store while ensuring state isn't lost if the app restarts?
If you were to add Redis into the mix, how would your read/write state resolution hierarchy (RAM -> Redis -> Disk) work under load?
day_7: How would you implement TTL-based expiry and background cleanup for stored sessions?
Describe how you would recover an active interview session after a process restart using layered persistence.
day_8: How do you decide between synchronous and asynchronous communication between microservices?
What resilience patterns would you apply so one failing service doesn't cascade into the whole system?
day_9: When would you choose a relational database over a key-value store like Redis, and why?
How do you model one-to-many relationships with SQLAlchemy, and what are indexes used for?
day_10: What mechanisms would you use to rate-limit an API and protect it from abuse?
How do you configure CORS safely and centralize logging across requests?
day_11: In your own words, how do transformer models work, and what is the role of attention?
What are tokens, and why do context windows matter when picking an LLM for your application?
day_12: How do you implement robust fallback mechanisms when external LLM APIs experience latency or 5xx errors?
How would you enforce timeouts and retries when calling an LLM asynchronously from FastAPI?
day_13: How do you design a system prompt that keeps an interviewer persona consistent across turns?
When would you use few-shot examples in a prompt, and what does chain-of-thought reasoning help with?
day_14: How do you force an LLM to return structured JSON and then validate it against a Pydantic schema?
What guardrails would you add to detect and prevent hallucinated technical claims?
day_15: How would you build a deterministic fallback question bank and when would it be served?
Describe how your interview agent degrades gracefully when the LLM times out mid-conversation.
day_16: What metrics would you use to evaluate whether interview questions are relevant to the curriculum?
How would you measure the hallucination rate of an LLM on interview transcripts?
day_17: How does edge-tts generate natural neural speech, and how would you stream that audio to a browser?
What are the tradeoffs of using the Web Speech API for transcribing a candidate's spoken answer?
day_18: How do you persist multi-turn conversation state and trim it to fit a token window?
How would you switch the interviewer persona between a hiring manager and a senior engineer across turns?
day_19: Walk me through the retrieval-augmented generation pipeline: indexing, retrieval, and generation.
What kind of content would you index so interview questions stay grounded in the curriculum?
day_20: How do embedding models represent text, and how is cosine similarity used to find relevant chunks?
What is an HNSW index, and how do its parameters affect vector search speed and accuracy?
day_21: What chunking strategies would you use to split a long curriculum document for retrieval?
How can metadata filters and reranking improve retrieval precision?
day_22: How do you ground an LLM's answer in source material and attach citations?
How would you verify that a technical claim in a generated question actually appears in the curriculum?
day_23: Describe how you would build an end-to-end RAG Q&A assistant and stream its answers to the UI.
What edge cases would you handle when retrieval returns no relevant chunks?
day_24: Why would you combine keyword search with vector search, and what does BM25 contribute?
How do you rank hybrid retrieval results to surface the most relevant evidence first?
day_25: How would you write a Dockerfile for a FastAPI app, and what is a multi-stage build?
How do you orchestrate a multi-service stack (API, Redis, ChromaDB) with docker-compose?
day_26: How would you set up CI/CD with GitHub Actions to test and deploy this interview agent?
How do you manage environment variables and secrets across dev and production safely?
day_27: How would you profile a slow FastAPI endpoint and find the async bottleneck?
What caching strategies would you apply to reduce latency under load, and how would you load test them?
day_28: What logs, metrics, and traces would you collect to observe an interview service in production?
How would you set up a health endpoint and alerting when the LLM dependency goes down?
day_29: How would you validate curriculum and candidate JSON at startup so bad data never reaches the app?
What is data drift, and how would you detect it in the curriculum content over time?
day_30: How would you mitigate bias in AI-generated interview questions, and what safety guardrails matter most?
How would you optimize the token cost of a full interview session without hurting question quality?
day_31: Describe how you would integrate FastAPI, Redis, ChromaDB, and edge-tts into one complete interview agent.
How would you ensure every interview session covers at least 4 different curriculum days, and how would you demo it?
